summary: VPC ENI secondary IP exhaustion causes persistent gRPC connection stickiness and control-plane latency
description: Issue summary: Customer reports increased control-plane latency and repeated gRPC client reconnects beginning 2026-03-10 08:20 UTC. Impact: model pulls and stream startups stall for a subset of serving nodes; customer sees longer tail latency and tokenization errors on active connections. Hypothesis: underlying VPC ENI secondary IP exhaustion on private deployment NAT/egress subnets is causing source IP reuse and gRPC connection sticky behavior, breaking connection pooling and control-plane callbacks.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Deploy private package in BrightFleet VPC with default ENI/secondary-ip allocation (subnet size /27).
2) Ramp to ~1200 concurrent short-lived connections (streaming chat start/stop cycles) from serving nodes to control-plane and artifact S3 endpoint,
3) Observe gRPC reconnects and streaming stalls after ~40 minutes,
4) Run 'aws ec2 describe-network-interfaces' and inspect PrivateIpAddresses list on ENIs attached to serving autoscaling group.
logs: aws ec2 describe-network-interfaces --filters 'Name=attachment.instance-owner-id,Values=aws' returned several ENIs with PrivateIpAddresses count at allocation=16/16 (full)
tcpdump: 10:08:21.123456 IP 10.0.4.12.51234 > 34.192.11.8.443: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240, options [mss 1460,sackOK,TS val 12345 ecr 0,nop,wscale 7], length 0
kernel: conntrack: table full, dropping packet (nf_conntrack overflow) seen at 10:20:43 on serving-node-02
gRPC logs (serving): 'HTTP/2 stream failed with io.grpc.StatusRuntimeException: UNAVAILABLE: connection terminated', repeated 4xx times per minute on affected nodes
control-plane: auth callback timed out after 5s for instance i-0abcde12345 (node reusing NAT port)'
investigation_notes: Initial triage: spikes in ephemeral port reuse and conntrack table saturation coincide with ENI secondary IP pools at max allocation in BrightFleet subnets.

ENI allocation pattern: autoscaling scaled to 8 nodes but subnets were /28 sized (16 addresses); third-party infra also hosts CI runners in same subnets, reducing available secondaries for Redwood ENIs.

Observed symptom: NAT gateway/source-NAT reuse leads to multiple distinct node TCP flows sharing same external source IP and ephemeral ports, causing gRPC connection stickiness and occasional misrouting of long-lived streams when source mapping changes mid-stream.
Control-plane effect: heavy re-use leads to backend perceiving stale TLS sessions and dropping connections; clients attempt reconnects, increasing load and exacerbating ENI/conntrack pressure.
Temporary mitigation tested: scaled up ENI available IPs by moving portion of nodes into adjacent /24 (customer network change) which immediately reduced reconnects; confirmed correlation.

root_cause: Customer VPC subnets used for Redwood serving nodes had insufficient available secondary IPs per ENI (small CIDR /28) combined with other tenant workloads in same subnets, leading to ENI secondary IP exhaustion, conntrack/NAT port reuse, and gRPC session instability.
resolution: Immediate: Guided customer to move serving nodes into larger CIDR subnets and isolate Redwood serving ENIs to dedicated subnets; recommended bursting nodes across additional subnets to avoid single-subnet exhaustion. Medium-term: created internal ticket to add a preflight check in private deployment installer to fail fast if subnet available IPs per AZ < recommended threshold and emit console warning. Follow-ups: update private deploy quickstart, add ENI allocation guidance to documentation, and track feature request to support alternate NAT mode that preserves 1:1 source IP mapping for long-lived gRPC sessions.
